public_health_question.v: Can traveler-based genomic surveillance at U.S. airports give early detection of new SARS-CoV-2 variants such as BA.2.86 entering the United States?

ev.q: TGS program was developed to provide early warning of new variants entering the United States by collecting samples from arriving international travelers
Early Identification of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2.86 Variant by the Traveler-Based Genomic Surveillance Program
As a component of comprehensive U.S. SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance, TGS detected the BA.2.86 variant within days of its first identification globally
The sample was collected from a U.S. resident returning from a 15–30-day trip to Japan
The TGS program anonymously collects two nasal swab samples from consenting international travelers arriving at six major U.S. airports.

equity.level_reason: A single detection in one traveler; no social-position dimension is analyzed or framed.

notes: A single-case detection report: the phylogenetic analysis (maximum likelihood tree, 1,000 bootstraps, HKY+F+I model) characterizes the case's genome and is not recorded as a procedure. The 95% decline in sequence submissions is cited from the GISAID dashboard. The prepass 'sensitivity' cue refers to antibody neutralization, not diagnostic accuracy.
